home.learnText: Play with Clef and learn music and code, step by step.
home.composeText: Make anything you like with every block. No lessons.

map.title: Pick a lesson
map.locked: Finish the lesson before this one to open it

studio.codeEmpty: Put a block inside My song to see its code here.
studio.codeExplain: This is real Strudel code. Your blocks wrote it!
studio.staffEmpty: Put a beat or a melody inside My song to see it written as music.
studio.staffExplain: This is your song written on a staff, the way musicians read music.
studio.drumKey: On a drum staff, each sound has its own line or space.
studio.emptySong: Put a block inside My song first!
studio.error: Hmm, that didn't work. Try changing a block.

tooltips.song: Everything inside My song plays when you press Play.
tooltips.sound: Plays one sound, once every bar. Code: s("bd")
tooltips.beat4: Four steps. Tap a square to turn it on or off. Code: s("bd ~ bd ~")
tooltips.beat8: Eight quick steps. Code: s("hh hh hh hh hh hh hh hh")
tooltips.melody: Put notes inside to play a tune. Code: note("c4 e4 g4")
tooltips.note: One note. Pick how high it is and how long it lasts.

clef.hello: Hi {name}! I'm Clef. Let's make music!
clef.helloNoName: Hi! I'm Clef. Let's make music!
clef.lessonDone: You finished the lesson! You earned a star!
clef.compose: Make anything you like! Press Play to hear it.

listen.say: Let's listen first! Press the big ear button.

drag.say: Find the pink play block. Drag it inside My song.
drag.hint: The pink block is on the left. Drop it just under My song, so it clicks in.

play.say: Now press the green Play button at the top!
play.hint: The Play button is green with a triangle.

change.say: Tap the little arrow on your block and pick a different sound. Try the sheep!
change.hint: Tap the word kick on your block. A list of sounds pops up.

card.musicText: Every instrument makes its own special sound. A drum sounds different to a sheep!
card.codeText: s() is a function: an instruction that does a job. This one plays a sound.

listen.say: This is a beat. Clap along with it! Press the ear button.

drag.say: Drag the purple beat block, the one with squares, inside My song.
drag.hint: It's the purple block with four squares.

fill.say: Tap all four squares to turn them on.
fill.hint: Tap each grey square once. It turns white when it's on.

play.say: Press Play. Can you hear four kicks? That's the beat!

code.say: Look at the code. Each kick is written as b d. Four kicks, one after another. That's called a sequence!
code.hint: The code is on the right side.

card.musicText: The beat is the steady pulse you can clap or march along to.
card.codeText: "bd bd bd bd" is a sequence: steps that happen one after another.

listen.say: Listen. Some steps are quiet! A quiet step is called a rest.

drag.say: Drag a beat block inside My song.

pattern.say: Turn on only the first and the third squares.
pattern.hint: On, off, on, off. Tap a white square to turn it off.

play.say: Press Play. Boom, rest, boom, rest. Can you hear the gaps?

code.say: In the code, a rest is a squiggle. Can you find the squiggles?
code.hint: They are glowing yellow in the code.

own.say: Now make your own rhythm! Leave at least one square off.
own.hint: Tap squares on and off until you like how it sounds.

card.musicText: A rest is a moment of silence. Sounds and rests together make a rhythm.
card.codeText: ~ is a symbol. In Strudel it means: be quiet for one step.

listen.say: This is a rock beat. Three instruments are playing at the same time!

kick.say: Put a beat block inside My song. Make it kick on squares one and three.
kick.hint: Pick the drum, then turn on the first and third squares.

snare.say: Add another beat block underneath. Pick the snare, and turn on squares two and four.
snare.hint: Tap kick on the new block and choose snare.

hats.say: Now add the long blue beat block. Pick the hi-hat, and turn on all eight squares.
hats.hint: The blue block has eight squares. The hi-hat has a top hat.

play.say: Press Play. You made a rock beat!

code.say: See the word stack in the code? Stack means: play these together.
code.hint: Stack is glowing at the top of the code.

card.musicText: When instruments play at the same time, the music sounds bigger and fuller.
card.codeText: stack() plays patterns side by side, all at once. Programmers call this running in parallel.

listen.say: Listen. These notes go up, like walking up stairs!

melody.say: Drag the green melody block inside My song.
melody.hint: It's the green block with a gap inside.

notes.say: Put three notes inside the melody. Red C, then orange D, then yellow E.
notes.hint: Drag the red note in first. Then orange, then yellow underneath.

staff.say: Tap the Staff button to see your music written down!
staff.hint: The Staff button is at the top of the right side.

look.say: These five lines are called a staff. Higher notes sit higher on the staff. C sits on its own little line underneath!
look.hint: Look at the red, orange and yellow notes climbing.

play.say: Press Play and sing along: C, D, E!

card.musicText: Music is written on five lines called a staff. Higher notes sit higher up.
card.codeText: note() plays notes by name. c4 is the C in the middle of the piano.

listen.say: Listen. Some notes are long, and some are short.

notes.say: Make a melody with at least two notes.
notes.hint: Drag the melody block in, then put notes inside it.

half.say: Change one note to a half note. It lasts two beats. On the staff it has an empty, hollow head!
half.hint: Tap the word quarter on a note and choose half.

whole.say: Now try a whole note. It lasts four beats, and it has no stick!
whole.hint: Tap quarter or half on a note and choose whole.

fill.say: Fill one bar: make your notes add up to exactly four beats.
fill.hint: A whole note is 4 beats. A half note is 2. A quarter note is 1.

play.say: Press Play and count along: one, two, three, four!

code.say: In the code, the at sign makes a note longer. A bigger number means a longer note.
code.hint: The at signs are glowing yellow.

card.musicText: Whole = 4 beats. Half = 2 beats. Quarter = 1 beat. Eighth = half a beat.
card.codeText: In c4@2, the @ makes that note last twice as long as the others.
